front: When is a pre-cardioversion TEE indicated for atrial fibrillation?
back: AF duration > 48 hours (or unknown) without therapeutic anticoagulation for at least 3 weeks. TEE rules out LA/LAA thrombus, allowing safe cardioversion.

front: Why should anticoagulation be continued for ≥ 4 weeks after cardioversion even if sinus rhythm is restored?
back: Atrial mechanical stunning persists for several weeks after electrical restoration of sinus rhythm — the atrium remains a thrombogenic environment.

front: State four echo parameters used to assess elevated LV filling pressure in patients with AF.
back: 1) DT < 160 ms with reduced EF. 2) E acceleration rate > 1900 cm/s². 3) IVRT ≤ 65 ms. 4) E/e′ ≥ 11. Also TR peak velocity, LAVI. Cannot use E/A (no A wave).

front: Post-Watchman LAAC device: what perileak size is considered clinically significant?
back: A peri-device leak > 5 mm is considered significant and typically warrants continuation of anticoagulation.

front: What is atrial stunning after cardioversion or PVI?
back: Transient reduction in mechanical atrial contraction despite return of electrical sinus rhythm. Manifests as an attenuated or absent A wave and represents a period of ongoing thromboembolic risk (4+ weeks post-conversion).
